title: PacTech Pulse: August 2026
gist: A roundup of June-July 2026 Indo-Pacific tech policy moves shows AI governance frameworks proliferating across Australia, China, Japan, Korea, and Southeast Asia, alongside new data-center energy/water mandates, semiconductor export controls and localization pushes, and quantum-safe cryptography planning.

themes.theme: AI governance frameworks across the Indo-Pacific

insights.claim: Australia announced an AI Framework establishing an Office of AI within the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, with a firm commitment to protect Australian creative works from being used to train AI models without consent.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A creative-works consent requirement in AI training is a compliance flag for any AI developer sourcing Australian content.
insights.locator: Australia announces an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Framework

insights.claim: Australia also outlined AI Consumer Safety Priorities across five areas — duty of care, privacy, AI safety in the workplace, consumer protections, and a framework for automated decision-making — to increase accountability and ensure safe adoption.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Signals upcoming Australian consumer-protection rulemaking specifically targeting automated decision-making, relevant to fintech and HR-tech AI deployers.
insights.locator: Australia outlines AI Consumer Safety Priorities

insights.claim: China released an Action Plan on AI Cooperation and Development aimed at strengthening international AI collaboration and bridging the global digital divide.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Part of China's push to position itself as an alternative AI-diplomacy hub for developing markets, competing with U.S.-aligned AI governance efforts.
insights.locator: China releases an Action Plan on Artificial Intelligence

insights.claim: China released a separate Action Plan on International AI Ethics Governance calling on countries to adopt categorized, tiered risk prevention and agile governance mechanisms and cultivate a collaborative AI ecosystem.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: China is actively exporting its own AI governance template globally, a soft-power vector to track alongside its industrial AI exports.
insights.locator: China releases an Action Plan on International AI Ethics Governance

insights.claim: China released a draft National Standard for Security Classification and Grading Method for Cybersecurity Technology and AI Applications addressing AI agent risks including data leakage, uncontrolled permissions, tool misuse, and actions deviating from user intent.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A formal domestic classification standard for agentic-AI risk in China suggests tightening compliance requirements ahead for AI agent deployers in the Chinese market.
insights.locator: China releases draft National Standard for Security Classification

insights.claim: Japan released a second AI Basic Plan aimed at accelerating deployment of smart technologies to address national challenges while enhancing regulatory frameworks and managing risks including cybersecurity threats.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Marks Japan's second iteration of national AI strategy, indicating continuity and escalation of state-directed AI adoption.
insights.locator: Japan releases a second Artificial Intelligence Basic Plan

insights.claim: Malaysia launched the Malaysia Digital Action Plan 2030 (MD2030), a five-year national roadmap placing the Ministry of Digital at the center of efforts to become an 'AI-driven nation' by 2030, spanning economic growth, digital public services, infrastructure, talent, cybersecurity, and AI innovation.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A comprehensive multi-year digital/AI roadmap positions Malaysia as a target market for AI infrastructure and talent investment through 2030.
insights.locator: Malaysia launches the Malaysia Digital Action Plan 2030

insights.claim: Singapore introduced voluntary transparency guidelines for generative AI chatbots, standardizing how companies explain capabilities, limitations, and risks to consumers and consolidating information currently scattered across privacy notices and terms of service.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Sets a disclosure bar for GenAI chatbot deployers in Singapore that could become a regional model, similar to how Singapore's earlier fintech guidelines influenced ASEAN peers.
insights.locator: Singapore introduces voluntary transparency guidelines

insights.claim: South Korea announced a national strategy to foster 'Physical AI' — AI capable of autonomous judgment and action in robotics and manufacturing — centered on data, technology, diffusion, and ecosystem.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Positions South Korea's robotics and manufacturing sectors as a direct national-strategy priority for embodied/physical AI investment.
insights.locator: South Korea announces a national strategy to foster

insights.claim: South Korea released an AI Basic Healthcare Strategy to introduce AI support for regional clinics, emergency patient transport, and public hospital operations, addressing patient concentration in Seoul-area hospitals and medical staff shortages.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Opens a concrete near-term procurement channel for AI-in-healthcare vendors targeting regional Korean public health infrastructure.
insights.locator: South Korea releases an AI Basic Healthcare Strategy

insights.claim: South Korea released a national strategy to develop 'Physical AI Ports,' with Gwangyang Port as a technology testbed and Jinhae New Port as the flagship AI-enabled port for autonomous equipment operation and optimized cargo logistics.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Names two specific Korean ports as pilot sites for AI-enabled port automation, relevant to logistics-tech and port-automation vendors.
insights.locator: South Korea releases a national strategy to develop

insights.claim: Thailand released a revised draft AI Act adopting a risk-based approach influenced by the EU AI Act, tailored to Thailand's legal and economic priorities, with obligations extending beyond Thailand's borders and new compliance requirements for higher-risk AI systems.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: An EU-AI-Act-style regime with extraterritorial reach means non-Thai AI vendors serving Thai users may face new compliance obligations.
insights.locator: Thailand releases a revised draft AI Act

insights.claim: South Korea announced a Manufacturing AI 2030 Strategy to integrate AI across core manufacturing industries including semiconductors, automobiles, and shipbuilding.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Ties Korea's flagship export industries (chips, autos, shipbuilding) directly to a national AI-adoption timeline through 2030.
insights.locator: South Korea announces its Manufacturing AI 2030 Strategy

insights.claim: Vietnam published its first official list of 46 high-risk AI systems that pose significant risks to life, health, rights, public/national interests, or national security, requiring providers and operators to meet stricter governance and conformity assessment before deployment.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Gives AI vendors operating in Vietnam a concrete compliance checklist (46 named high-risk system categories) ahead of enforcement.
insights.locator: Vietnam publishes its first official list of 46 high-risk AI systems

insights.claim: Australia's new Standards for AI will require large-scale data centers to underwrite new power generation and contribute at least as much energy to the national grid as they consume, plus water-efficiency obligations and full-cost payment for grid and water infrastructure connections.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: A net-positive-generation requirement for data centers materially raises the capital cost of building hyperscale AI infrastructure in Australia, a template other grid-constrained markets may copy.
insights.locator: Australia announces the Australian Standards for AI

insights.claim: Thailand revised its screening policy for data-center investments to assess projects across electricity supply/energy readiness, water-resource management, environmental protection/pollution controls, and tangible benefit to Thailand and resource efficiency.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Adds a formal multi-factor investment-screening gate for data centers in Thailand, a factor for hyperscalers evaluating Southeast Asian AI-infrastructure siting.
insights.locator: Thailand revises its screening policy for Data Center investments

insights.claim: Bangladesh published comprehensive guidelines for developing onshore wind-power projects to help it pursue ambitious renewable-energy targets.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Establishes a formal regulatory framework opening Bangladesh's onshore wind sector to developer investment.
insights.locator: Bangladesh publishes comprehensive guidelines

insights.claim: China unveiled a roadmap dubbed AI for Accelerator-Driven Advanced Nuclear Energy Systems (ADANES) to integrate AI with the full life cycle of advanced nuclear energy systems, aiming for zero tolerance for safety failures.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Signals China's push to pair AI with next-generation nuclear technology, a potential export capability for advanced reactor markets.
insights.locator: China unveils a roadmap that integrates artificial intelligence

insights.claim: China added 14 European entities to its export control list, prohibiting Chinese exporters from supplying them with dual-use items including rare earths and permanent magnets without special authorization, citing national security and non-proliferation obligations.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Direct, immediate supply-chain risk for named European firms dependent on Chinese rare earths and permanent magnets — a live escalation in China's export-control toolkit.
insights.locator: China adds 14 European entities to its export control list

insights.claim: South Korea published a pan-government strategy to accelerate localization of defense semiconductors and secure a stable supply chain, centered on a full-cycle framework linking demand, development, verification, and mass production through public-private cooperation.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Opens a new domestic-sourcing mandate track for Korean defense-semiconductor suppliers as the government builds a demand-to-production pipeline.
insights.locator: South Korea publishes a pan-government strategy

insights.claim: Thailand unveiled the Siam Silica Framework, a roadmap to build a domestic semiconductor ecosystem and position the country as a hub in an integrated ASEAN supply chain, targeting photonics fabrication, advanced packaging, silicon design, quantum photonics, and power devices.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Names five specific semiconductor sub-sectors Thailand is targeting for ASEAN-hub positioning, relevant for chip-supply-chain diversification plays.
insights.locator: Thailand unveils the Siam Silica Framework

insights.claim: South Korea announced plans to ease regulations allowing biopharmaceutical CDMOs to produce products in line with overseas clients' regulatory standards rather than only domestic facility standards, reducing companies' burden in global contract processes.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: Lowers a regulatory barrier for Korean CDMOs competing for international biopharma manufacturing contracts.
insights.locator: South Korea announces plans to ease regulations

insights.claim: Malaysia published a National Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration Plan and a Quantum Cryptography Sandbox to safeguard the country against future cyber threats posed by quantum computing and build a robust national cryptography ecosystem.
insights.speaker: CSIS
insights.so_what: One of the region's earliest formal post-quantum cryptography migration frameworks, a marker for enterprises assessing quantum-readiness timelines in Southeast Asia.
insights.locator: Malaysia publishes a National Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration Plan
